name: America's Green Airline (Powered by Pratt & Whitney)
description: Frontier's A321neo N603FR, 'Frederick the Bald Eagle', in a green special promoting its Pratt & Whitney GTF engines: the front of the fuselage white with the usual green 'FRONTIER' titles; over the wing the white fades through a pale mint into a deep green that covers the whole rear fuselage, the fin and the engines; 'America's Green Airline' in lime green over the rear windows and 'POWERED BY PRATT & WHITNEY' in white under them; the bald eagle spreads its wings across the green fin, its head and talons painted on the rear fuselage round the aft door; lime sharklets. No teal line or web address. N604FR ('Maria the Bald Eagle') and N605FR ('Edward the Bald Eagle') wear the same scheme with their own eagles on the fin (open photos 2023 and 2026).

mint.name: the fade's middle, white to green

areas.name: the fade's pale middle over the wing root (white to mint to green), drawn as one band with straight, upright edges
deep green from over the wing to the tail, crown to belly

logos.description: Frederick the bald eagle, photographic: wings spread up the green fin toward its tip, its white head and yellow beak and its talons painted on the rear fuselage either side of the aft door (the art runs down off the fin). No sky behind it, as on the standard tails: the fin's ground is the scheme's green.
A small US flag after the registration over the rear windows.

titles.style: Frontier's wordmark, as on the standard scheme (measured there on N638FR; it sits the same on N603FR's photos, x 0.13 to 0.45).
Lime-green bold geometric sans, mixed case, over the rear windows from just behind the wing's root to ahead of the registration.
White condensed capitals under the rear windows, regular weight; 'PRATT & WHITNEY' follows in bold.

notes: Drawn on three open photos of N603FR (2022-12 left side-on, 2023-07 left through tinted glass, 2024-11 right), each fitted to the measured A321neo shape. The fade from white to green runs over the wing's root: white to about x 0.415 at the crown and below the windows, full green from about 0.49; drawn as one mint band (0.425 to 0.465) between white and green with upright straight edges. The belly under the fade is hidden by the engine and gear in every photo: the edges are carried down upright, not seen. The right side matches the left (titles over the same stretch; on the right 'N603FR' comes before 'America's' from the tail). The eagle is per-jet art (airframes/FFT.json `art`); its head and talons on the rear fuselage are left to the art, not drawn as areas. The animal's name under the cockpit ('Frederick THE BALD EAGLE') and the registration aren't drawn. Currency: N603FR flies (adsb.lol 2026-11-13); the newest open photo of the paint is 2024-11-01, and a spotter lead lists it in 2026.
